ww.Papillary thyroid carcinoma: Papillary carcinoma shows branching papillae with optically clear, grooved nuclei, not round follicles full of colloid.
ww.Graves disease follicles: Graves follicles are lined by tall hyperplastic cells with pale, scalloped colloid from rapid hormone release.
ww.Hashimoto thyroiditis: Hashimoto thyroiditis shows lymphoid follicles with germinal centers and pink Hurthle cells replacing the follicles.
ww.Medullary thyroid carcinoma: Medullary carcinoma is sheets of parafollicular C cells with amyloid stroma, not colloid-filled follicles.

look: Round follicles lined by a single layer of flat to cuboidal cells, each filled with a lake of pink colloid. The colloid is stored thyroglobulin, waiting for TSH to trigger its endocytosis and the release of T4 and T3.
cred: Synthetic test image made for the engine test bed
findings: A colloid-filled follicle, the storage lake of thyroglobulin
The single layer of follicular cells lining it

ann.l: Colloid-filled follicle. The pink lake is thyroglobulin stored outside the cells, waiting for TSH to trigger its endocytosis.
Follicular cell layer. A single row of cuboidal cells traps iodide and makes thyroglobulin; they grow tall when TSH or Graves antibodies stimulate them.
Follicle diameter. Large, colloid-rich follicles mean hormone is being stored rather than released quickly.
Whole-field pattern. Uniform round follicles with no papillae and no lymphoid infiltrate is the normal architecture.
